data.name: Celene
data.gender_notes: Celene is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'selene', meaning 'moon'. In Greek mythology, Selene was the goddess of the moon, revered for her cyclical nature and the influence she had on tides and growth. The name Celene carries the meaning “Moon goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Celene usually hope their child will grow to embody moon goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine feminine and the cyclical nature of life.
data.etymology: Celene belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon goddess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Celene total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
data.cultural_impact: Celene, as a name, invokes the image of the moon goddess Selene, that decorated pottery, coins, and architecture in ancient Greece. She was associated with the creative cycle of life, and the name Celene could encourage a sense of artistic imagery, inspiration, and connection to the natural world.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Celene holds relevance to the spiritual realm as it comes from the ancient Greek mythology of Selene, the goddess of the moon. Naming a child Celene could represent a desire to encourage an enchanted, imaginative spirit and emphasize the connection to the ebb and flow of nature and its cycles. In Christianity, it could also be seen as a reminder of the cyclical nature of life, representing the Old and New Testaments, or a way to acknowledge the underlying presence and support of the Divine through the trials and changes that human life comprises.
